title: Policy-driven retention engine for telemetry and evidence packaging
creator: Elena Rodriguez
description:
Problem: Customers (esp. regulated enterprises) need fine-grained, auditable controls for how long different categories of inference data are retained and where that data resides. Current platform offerings have coarse retention defaults and manual evidence exports, which complicates compliance assessments and increases legal risk.

Goal: Design and ship a policy-driven retention engine that lets administrators declare retention rules by data class (prompts, responses, request logs/headers, metrics/telemetry, embeddings, KV cache snapshots), tenancy/residency, and purpose. The system must enforce deletion/redaction/aggregation semantics, produce machine-readable evidence bundles for audits, integrate with residency constraints (region-specific storage), and expose admin UI + API for configuration and reporting.

Success metrics: (1) Ability for customers to configure retention rules covering all major data classes; (2) Evidence export that demonstrates retention enforcement for a given time window (audit-ready bundle) with <24h SLA for bundle generation; (3) No customer-facing incidents caused by retention enforcement; (4) Positive feedback from at least two pilot enterprise customers validating policy UI and evidence exports.
acceptance_criteria: Admin console exposes retention policy builder: rules scoped to tenant, project, route, or model label; choose data classes (prompt, response, request-log, metrics, embedding, kv-snapshot)
Policies support common actions: delete, redact (token masking), aggregate (retain histograms), and move-to-cold (encrypted S3 bucket in specified region)
Per-policy residency constraint (region or 'global') is respected for all data motion and evidence bundles
Retention engine records immutable enforcement events (timestamped) that are includable in audit bundles
API endpoints to create/list/update/validate policies and to request on-demand evidence export (job status + download URL)
Background workers implement retention enforcement with metrics and backfill ability; enforcement errors surface to Console and to SLA alerts
Migration path for existing stored data: dry-run validation mode and one-click enforce for historical partitions
Security review completed and KMS/HSM usage documented for any exported evidence bundles
implementation_notes:
High level approach: 1) Define canonical data-class taxonomy and extend metadata on all request events with retention-policy pointers. 2) Implement a policy-reconciliation service that compiles admin rules into enforcement jobs (per-tenant job graph). 3) Enforcement actions are idempotent: delete (hard delete from primary store + tombstone in index), redact (replace sensitive fields with deterministic mask), aggregate (compute and store aggregated metrics in a retention-safe store). 4) Evidence packaging service collects enforcement events, sample traces, and manifests (checksums) and signs bundles; store bundles in customer-residency-compliant buckets. 5) Integrations: S3 lifecycle rules, BigQuery table partition TTLs, and object-store cold-tier API for large archives.

Data model changes required (examples): add retention_policy_id and retention_effective_at to request_log rows; annotate embeddings with tenant_retention_tier.

Operational concerns: scale enforcement across high-throughput tenants without impacting serving latency. Enforce rate-limited background workers and backpressure to avoid I/O storms. Provide throttles and canary rollout per tenant.

Edge cases: on-demand evidence for deleted items should include cryptographic manifest proving deletion (checksums of prior index and deletion event), not the deleted content itself. For requests subject to legal hold, support retention hold flag that overrides normal expiry until cleared.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal alpha 6 weeks): CLI and API-only retention rules; run against synthetic tenants and internal logs; verify enforcement correctness and metrics. Phase 2 (private beta 8 weeks): UI builder in Console, per-tenant residency constraints, evidence export job; onboard 2 pilot customers (Dedicated or Private) and iterate. Phase 3 (general availability 4 weeks after beta): enable for hosted customers behind a feature flag; provide migration tools and migration-runbook; announce in release notes and update docs.

Monitoring + SLOs: enforcement job success rate >= 99.5% per day; evidence bundle generation SLA < 24h (target < 6h for small tenants). Rollback plan: disable enforcement jobs at tenant scope; restore pre-retention index from tombstone logs if needed (requires support-runbook).
